query: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes June 24 confirmed death toll latest figures, trajectory of confirmed deaths reported by authorities and Wikipedia, number of missing persons and rescue operation status
answer:
Research complete. The key findings:

**Death toll:** The latest official confirmed figure is **6,438**, announced Monday 17 August 2026 by National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez. The trajectory is decelerating: +579 (24 Jul→3 Aug, 10 days), +176 (3→10 Aug), +137 (10→17 Aug). Updates now come as a **weekly Monday bulletin** of the *Plan Venezuela Renace*, so the next is due 24 August. Increases now come almost entirely from body recovery during debris removal, not new fatalities.

**Wikipedia:** The infobox raw wikitext holds the exact official values (6,438 and 86,358) but applies `rounddown` to the nearest 100, displaying ">6,400 dead, ~86,300 injured, c.18,100–50,000 missing." Two caveats worth flagging: it lags the official number by up to 99 through rounding, and it mislabels the hospital-treatment count as "injured" — the official injured figure is 16,740 and has been frozen since early July.

**Missing:** No reliable figure exists, and that gap is deliberate. The only national official number ever published is **157** from 25 June, never updated; Rodríguez says the government withholds it "to avoid speculation." Estimates elsewhere span two orders of magnitude — La Guaira's governor says 1,579, a diplomatic source told AFP "above 10,000," the UN aid chief's initial 50,000 was later called an error, and three crowdsourced trackers disagree with each other by ~20,000 (17,790 / 29,518 / 41,332). Venezuela's last census was 2011, so there's no population denominator to work from.

**Rescue status:** Live rescues total **6,462**, frozen since at least 3 August. Formal search-and-rescue ceased around 4 July; the operation is now body recovery, demolition and debris clearance. 528,222 tons removed nationally (25.15% of ~2.1M tons estimated). On 19 August, 20 remotely-operable machines donated by the US arrived at the Port of La Guaira, joining 700+ already deployed. Al Jazeera and the BBC document families and volunteers still leading recovery at some sites with hand tools, and demolition is contested by relatives still searching.

One structural point for interpretation: "deaths" and "missing" are converging categories rather than independent ones — each week's increment converts missing persons into confirmed deaths, and the governor noted some listed as missing are already dead but awaiting forensic certification.

key_facts: Latest official confirmed death toll from the 24 June 2026 Venezuela earthquake doublet is 6,438, announced Monday 17 August 2026 by National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez.
The 17 August figure was +137 over the previous week's 6,301 (10 Aug), which was +176 over 6,125 (3 Aug). The weekly increment is decelerating; the last two full weeks average ~156/week.

Official updates now come as a weekly 'Boletin Informativo Semanal' of the Plan Venezuela Renace 'Etapa de Reconstruccion', published on Mondays by Jorge Rodriguez via Telegram/X. Updates landed on Mondays 3, 10 and 17 August; the next is due Monday 24 August.
Reporting cadence has been irregular: there was a 10-day blackout between 24 July (5,546) and 3 August (6,125), which drew a formal demand for updates from the Venezuelan NGO Provea.

The bulletin format changed on 3 August, dropping the injured, displaced (damnificados) and collapsed-building counts and adding homes-delivered and debris-tonnage indicators. Those dropped series are now frozen at late-July values.
Deaths now rise almost entirely through body recovery during debris removal and demolition, not new fatalities.

English Wikipedia's infobox raw wikitext holds the exact official values 6,438 and 86,358, displayed with rounddown to the nearest 100 as '>6,400 dead, ~86,300 injured, c.18,100-50,000 missing', plus damage of US$37 billion.

Wikipedia labels 86,358 as 'injured', but the official metric is 'personas atendidas en hospitales' (cumulative people treated in hospitals). The official injured figure is 16,740 and has been frozen since early July.
The only national official missing-persons figure ever published is 157, from 25 June 2026 — never updated since. Jorge Rodriguez said the government withholds the figure 'to avoid speculation'.

La Guaira Governor Jose Alejandro Teran gave state-level missing figures of 1,338 (late July, from the Registro Unico de Viviendas, cutoff 29 July) and 1,579 (4 August, from direct family reports), cautioning some may already be dead but not yet certified by SENAMECF.
UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher estimated over 50,000 missing on 25 June; a diplomatic source told AFP this was an 'error' and that the working figure is 'above 10,000'.

Crowdsourced trackers disagree by ~20,000: Venezuela Te Busca (17,790 still to locate), Desaparecidos Terremoto Venezuela (29,518 'sin contacto'), Venezuela Reporta (41,332 missing as of 19 Aug, from 93,309 reports with 41,351 duplicates purged).
Venezuela's last census was in 2011, leaving no reliable population denominator for the affected zone; the AFP diplomatic source concluded 'there are no reliable figures' on the missing.

Live rescues total 6,462 and the figure has been frozen since at least 3 August. Most formal rescue operations ceased around 4 July (day 10); Spain, the Netherlands, Colombia and some US teams ended search operations in early July citing low survival probability.
Notable late survivors: security guard Hernan Gil pulled alive after 8 days (2 July); a 3-year-old after 6 days (1 July); two more found alive by local teams around 23 July.
Current phase is body recovery, demolition and debris clearance. 528,222.30 tons of debris removed nationally as of 17 August = 25.15% of the ~2.1 million tons estimated by UNDP.
On 19 August, 20 remotely-operable heavy machines donated by the US government arrived at the Port of La Guaira, joining 700+ heavy machines and 13,000+ FANB personnel already deployed in the state.

Families and volunteers continue leading body recovery at some sites with hand tools, reporting minimal state assistance; demolition of unstable buildings is contested by relatives still searching for remains.

190 buildings collapsed, 856 affected, 16,200+ structures classified unsafe, ~1,500 aftershocks recorded by 24 July. 59,109 homes evaluated by 17 August: 34,680 habitable, 13,733 restricted, 10,696 high-risk.
~24,000 people are living in temporary camps in La Guaira and Caracas; 335 homes have been delivered against a pledge of 4,000 by year-end.
